question.problem:
The basis $\mathcal{B}$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the matrix $[\,\mathbf{T}\,]_{\mathcal{B}}$ of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}: \mathbb{R}^3 \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^3$ relative to $\mathcal{B}$ are given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156741/assets/beb5fb8757faf2c9e25c46013b90565611943b2796b0f23c6f0dece1e44e9055.svg)

What is the value of $\,a+b+c,\,$ given that  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156741/assets/2f5d701e5ded2a62bdc85878a6d7b8e575bec05aabd7d4b132fac7e3bdbc5f3a.svg)
question.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ as $\{ \mathbf{b}_1,\mathbf{b}_2,\mathbf{b}_3 \}.$ The $\mathcal{B}$-matrix for $\mathbf{T}$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_1),$ $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_2),$ and $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_3)$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}.$

To find the coordinates of $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_1),$ $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_2),$ and $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_3)$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}$, we consider the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156741/assets/7136e2bb6e6f18a4bdb43a10ea3f14833077197b55bdd5bdc4c31c2aca7be2ab.svg)

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $\mathcal{B}$-matrix for $\mathbf{T}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & -9 & 7 & 10 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 0 & -2 & -10 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 4 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & -9 & 7 & 10 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 0 & -2 & -10 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & -9 & 7 & 10 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156741/assets/2eba20e60b23942d9074b2e88003bee36267b40381f3fa157b1f74e38bef5198.svg)

Finally, $a=1,$ $b=-2,$ $c=-2$ and 

$$
a+b+c = 1+(-2)+(-2) = -3.
$$
